name: Codenames
description: Two teams give one-word clues to identify agents while avoiding the assassin.

name: Dixit
description: Players tell imaginative clues for surreal art cards and score through clever guesses.

name: Love Letter
description: Quick deduction card game about delivering letters and eliminating rivals.

name: Dominion
description: Classic deck-building game where players buy cards to build stronger turns.

name: Betrayal at House on the Hill
description: Cooperative exploration turns into one-vs-many horror with unique scenario twists.

name: Sheriff of Nottingham
description: Bluff and negotiate goods through inspections while outsmarting the sheriff.

name: Decrypto
description: Teams send coded clues to teammates while intercepting opponent code patterns.

name: Skull
description: Simple bluffing game of hidden skulls and flowers with escalating bids.

name: Exploding
description: Light take-that card game about avoiding explosive kittens with action cards.

name: Saboteur
description: Dwarves dig tunnels for gold while hidden saboteurs secretly block progress.

name: Wavelength
description: Teams guess where clues land on a spectrum for cooperative party scoring.

name: Mysterium
description: Ghost gives visual clues to mediums solving suspects locations and murder details.

name: Terraforming Mars
description: Engine-building strategy game where corporations develop Mars for human habitation.

name: Werewolf
description: Social deduction game with hidden roles and daytime voting accusations.

name: The Resistance
description: Players complete missions while spies sabotage and deceive the team.

name: Avalon
description: Arthurian Resistance variant with hidden roles and special powers for deduction.

name: Secret Hitler
description: Hidden roles and political voting game set in tense historical theme.

name: Coup
description: Fast bluffing card game of influence powers and challenge actions.

name: Settlers of Catan
description: Trade resources and build roads settlements to earn victory points.

name: Ticket to Ride
description: Collect train cards to claim routes and complete destination tickets.

name: carcasonne
description: Tile-laying game building cities roads and fields for area scoring.

name: Pandemic
description: Cooperative strategy to contain global outbreaks and discover disease cures.

name: Venus Flytrap
description: A carnivorous plant with trap-like leaves that snap shut when insects touch trigger hairs. Used for pest control botanical study and ornamental display.

name: Corpse Flower
description: Giant tropical flower that produces one of the largest blooms in the world and smells like rotting flesh. Used for botanical research greenhouse attractions and education about pollination.

name: Dragons Blood Tree
description: An umbrella-shaped tree that produces a deep red resin called dragons blood. Used in traditional medicine as dye varnish and incense.

name: Ghost Orchid
description: Rare orchid with floating white flowers that appear ghost-like in forests. Used for ornamental horticulture and conservation research.

name: Pitcher Plant
description: Carnivorous plant with tube-shaped leaves that trap insects in digestive liquid. Used for natural insect control and educational displays.

name: Mimosa pudica
description: Leaves fold inward quickly when touched. Used for educational demonstrations and as ornamental plant.

name: Baobab Tree
description: Massive tree with thick trunk that stores water and appears upside-down. Sacred in African traditional religions. Provides food from fruit pulp and offers traditional medicine fiber and shelter.

name: Jade Plant
description: Succulent with thick leaves often associated with prosperity. Rooted in Taoist feng shui symbolism for luck and good fortune. Used for indoor decoration.

name: Aloe Vera
description: Succulent with gel-filled leaves. Used for skin care burns treatment and cosmetics.

name: Stinging Nettle
description: Plant covered with tiny stinging hairs. Used for herbal tea medicine and textile fiber.

name: Mandrake
description: Plant with forked root historically linked to myths and magic. Mentioned in the Bible as a symbol of fertility and associated with ancient witchcraft traditions. Used in historical herbal medicine and folklore studies.

name: Bamboo
description: Fast-growing grass that can reach great heights. Used for construction furniture paper and food from bamboo shoots.

name: Lotus
description: Aquatic plant with large floating leaves and symbolic flowers. Sacred in Hinduism and Buddhism representing purity and spiritual enlightenment. Used for food from seeds and roots and in ornamental ponds.

name: Neem Tree
description: Tree revered in Hindu culture as a sacred healing plant. Known for strong medicinal and insect-repelling properties. Used as natural pesticide in medicine and skincare products.

name: Saffron Crocus
description: Flower whose stigmas produce the spice saffron. Used in religious ceremonies across ancient Persian and Greek traditions. Used as culinary spice dye and in traditional medicine.

name: Lavender
description: Aromatic herb with purple flowers. Used for essential oils perfumes relaxation products and cooking.

name: Ginkgo
description: Ancient tree species with fan-shaped leaves. Planted at Buddhist temples across Asia and considered sacred. Used for herbal supplements and urban landscaping.

name: Camellia sinensis
description: Evergreen shrub used to produce green black and oolong teas. Used for beverage production and antioxidants in health products.

name: Cocoa Tree
description: Tropical tree whose seeds produce chocolate. Used for chocolate production beverages and cosmetics.

name: Rubber Tree
description: Tree that produces latex sap. Used for natural rubber in tires gloves and industrial products.

name: Rafflesia
description: Parasitic plant producing the world's largest single flower known for its strong rotten smell. Used for botanical research eco-tourism and education about parasitic plants.

name: Monkey Puzzle Tree
description: Ancient conifer with stiff spiraling branches and sharp leaves. Used for ornamental landscaping and produces edible seeds.

name: Bleeding Heart
description: Plant with heart-shaped flowers that appear to drip from the bottom. Used for ornamental gardening.

name: Sundew
description: Carnivorous plant with sticky tentacles that trap insects. Used for botanical research and pest control in terrariums.

name: Walking Onion
description: Plant that forms bulb clusters that bend and walk across the ground. Provides edible onions and is a home gardening curiosity.

name: Tillandsia
description: Plant that grows without soil and absorbs nutrients from air and moisture. Used for indoor decoration and terrariums.

name: Welwitschia
description: Strange desert plant with only two leaves that grow continuously for centuries. Used for botanical research and desert ecosystem study.

name: Snake Plant
description: Hardy plant with tall sword-like leaves. Used for indoor air purification and houseplant decoration.

name: Prayer Plant
description: Leaves fold upward at night like hands in prayer. Used as indoor ornamental plant.

name: Ice Plant
description: Succulent with shiny cells on leaves that sparkle like ice crystals. Used for ground cover in gardens and erosion control.

name: Swiss Cheese Plant (Monstera)
description: Tropical plant with large leaves full of natural holes. Used for interior decoration and ornamental landscaping.

name: Curry Leaf Tree
description: Small tree with aromatic leaves used in cooking. Used as culinary spice and in traditional medicine.

name: Curry Plant (Helichrysum)
description: Plant with leaves that smell like curry but are rarely eaten. Used in aromatic gardens and for ornamental use.

name: Bottle Gourd
description: Climbing vine producing hard-shelled gourds. Used for containers musical instruments and utensils.

name: Ghost Pepper Plant
description: Plant that produces one of the world's hottest peppers. Used for extreme spice in cooking and hot sauces.

name: Chocolate Cosmos
description: Flower that naturally smells like chocolate. Used for ornamental gardening and fragrance gardens.

name: Corkscrew Vine
description: Vine with twisted spiral flowers. Used as decorative climbing plant.

name: Fairy Lantern
description: Plant with lantern-shaped flowers that grow close to the ground. Used for ornamental gardening.

name: Paperbark Tree
description: Australian tree with distinctive layered white bark that peels in thin papery sheets. Used in traditional Aboriginal medicine shelter construction and food wrapping.

name: Breadfruit Tree
description: Large tropical tree bearing starchy fruits that can be cooked and eaten. Important food staple in Pacific island communities used in cooking and traditional culture.

name: Marcus Aurelius
description: Roman Emperor and Stoic philosopher whose book Meditations shaped modern ideas of resilience self-discipline and mindful leadership. Widely read by world leaders and entrepreneurs today.

name: Seneca (4 BC–65 AD)
description: Roman Stoic philosopher and playwright whose writings on time management and the brevity of life directly influence modern productivity and self-improvement culture.

name: Epictetus (50–135 AD)
description: Former slave who became a Stoic philosopher. His teachings on focusing only on what we can control shaped cognitive behavioral therapy and modern resilience psychology.

name: Socrates (470–399 BC)
description: Ancient Greek philosopher known for the Socratic method of questioning. His approach to critical thinking forms the foundation of modern education legal reasoning and scientific inquiry.

name: Plato (427–347 BC)
description: Student of Socrates who founded the Academy in Athens. His theory of ideal forms and justice shaped Western philosophy politics and the concept of democracy.

name: Aristotle (384–322 BC)
description: Student of Plato who founded formal logic and classified knowledge into sciences. His work underpins modern biology ethics politics and the scientific method.

name: Confucius (551–479 BC)
description: Ancient Chinese philosopher and teacher whose emphasis on virtue education and social harmony continues to shape East Asian culture governance and family values.

name: Laozi (6th century BC)
description: Ancient Chinese philosopher and founder of Taoism whose text the Tao Te Ching shapes Eastern thought on balance harmony and non-interference influencing leadership and wellness today.

name: Zhuangzi (369–286 BC)
description: Taoist philosopher known for poetic philosophical writing whose ideas about perspective freedom and living naturally influence Eastern psychology and modern mindfulness practices.

name: Immanuel Kant (1724–1804)
description: German philosopher who defined the limits of reason and human knowledge. His categorical imperative shapes modern ethics human rights law and democratic political theory.

name: Friedrich Nietzsche (1844–1900)
description: German philosopher who challenged traditional morality and religion. His concepts of the will to power and self-overcoming influence modern psychology existentialism and cultural criticism.

name: Arthur Schopenhauer (1788–1860)
description: German philosopher known for the philosophy of will whose ideas influenced Freud and Nietzsche and shaped modern theories on desire motivation and the unconscious mind.

name: René Descartes (1596–1650)
description: French philosopher and mathematician who founded modern rationalism. His statement I think therefore I am anchors modern ideas of consciousness and the scientific method.

name: John Locke (1632–1704)
description: English philosopher who defined natural rights of life liberty and property. His political theory directly shaped the United States Constitution and modern liberal democracy.

name: David Hume (1711–1776)
description: Scottish philosopher who questioned causation and the limits of human reason. His empiricism influenced modern science economics and the philosophy of religion and mind.

name: Baruch Spinoza (1632–1677)
description: Dutch philosopher who argued for the unity of God and nature as a single substance. His ideas shaped secular thought the separation of church and state and modern pantheism.

name: Voltaire (1694–1778)
description: French Enlightenment writer and philosopher whose fierce advocacy for freedom of speech tolerance and secular governance helped ignite the French Revolution and modern civil liberties.

name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau (1712–1778)
description: French philosopher who argued society corrupts natural human goodness. His ideas about the social contract and popular sovereignty shaped modern democracy and education theory.

name: Thomas Hobbes (1588–1679)
description: English philosopher who argued that without government life would be brutal and short. His social contract theory laid the groundwork for modern political science and state authority.

name: John Stuart Mill (1806–1873)
description: British philosopher and economist known for utilitarianism and liberalism. His defense of individual freedom and women's rights influenced modern democracy and human rights legislation.

name: Karl Marx (1818–1883)
description: German philosopher and economist who analyzed capitalism and class struggle. His ideas shaped socialist and communist movements and continue to influence political economy and labor rights debate.

name: Simone de Beauvoir (1908–1986)
description: French existentialist philosopher and feminist whose book The Second Sex is a founding text of modern feminism challenging gender roles and shaping women's liberation movements worldwide.

name: Jean-Paul Sartre (1905–1980)
description: French existentialist philosopher who argued existence precedes essence. His ideas on radical freedom and personal responsibility profoundly shaped modern literature psychology and political activism.

name: Albert Camus (1913–1960)
description: French-Algerian philosopher and author who explored the absurdity of life. His philosophy of rebellion against meaninglessness continues to inspire modern ethics literature and humanist thought.

name: Ludwig Wittgenstein (1889–1951)
description: Austrian-British philosopher who revolutionized the philosophy of language. His insight that meaning depends on use in context shaped modern linguistics cognitive science and analytic philosophy.

name: Bertrand Russell (1872–1970)
description: British philosopher and mathematician whose work in mathematical logic helped birth modern computer science and artificial intelligence. A leading voice for pacifism and rationalism.

name: Hannah Arendt (1906–1975)
description: German-American political philosopher who analyzed totalitarianism and the nature of evil. Her work on political freedom and public life shapes modern debates on democracy authoritarianism and human rights.

name: Michel Foucault (1926–1984)
description: French philosopher who analyzed how power and knowledge shape social institutions. His critiques of prisons medicine and sexuality influence modern sociology critical theory and political activism.

name: Thomas Aquinas (1225–1274)
description: Medieval theologian and philosopher who synthesized Aristotle with Christian theology. His natural law theory underpins modern Catholic moral teaching and Western concepts of justice and human dignity.

name: Augustine of Hippo (354–430)
description: Early Christian theologian and philosopher whose ideas on sin grace and the City of God shaped Western Christianity. His introspective writing influenced modern psychology and religious philosophy.

name: Diogenes (412–323 BC)
description: Ancient Greek Cynic philosopher who lived in radical simplicity. His rejection of wealth and social convention challenges modern consumerism and inspires minimalist and anti-establishment thought.

name: Heraclitus (535–475 BC)
description: Pre-Socratic Greek philosopher who taught that everything is in constant flux. His ideas on change and opposing forces influenced Hegel Marx and modern process philosophy.

name: Parmenides (515–450 BC)
description: Pre-Socratic Greek philosopher who argued that reality is one unchanging whole. His reasoning against change and plurality shaped the foundations of Western metaphysics and logical argumentation.
